# Bundled runtime notices

Paper Factory bundles separate upstream runtimes and libraries. They retain their own licenses. The Paper Factory MIT license does not replace those terms.

- CPython 3.14.8: official Astral `python-build-standalone` release `20261003`, GIL-enabled `install_only_stripped` archives. The build catalog records each official archive SHA256 and release source commit. Original interpreter notices are preserved under `python/` and duplicated into `licenses/upstream/python/`. The complete upstream source notice set from the exact build commit is preserved separately in `licenses/python-build-standalone/`, including the dependency notices omitted by install-only archives. This set covers the upstream project's supported components; it does not claim that every listed component is loaded on every target.
- Node.js 24.21.0: official nodejs.org release archives verified against the existing repository's pinned SHA256 catalog. The complete Node license and embedded dependency notices are in `licenses/node/LICENSE`. npm is a build tool and is not part of this Node payload.
- Python dependencies: existing CPython 3.14 platform wheel pins from `desktop/runtime-inputs/host-dependencies.json`, with interpreter platform pins in `desktop/runtime-manifest.json`. Every downloaded wheel is size- and SHA256-verified, installed offline at build time, and recorded in `licenses/license-inventory.json`. Original distribution notices and license metadata are retained. pip is used only in the separate maintainer bootstrap; its installed package, distribution metadata and console launchers are excluded from application runtime payloads before the license and file inventories are generated.
- QuickJS: unchanged reviewed `quickjs-runtime.zip`, containing `quickjs-emscripten-core`, `@jitl/quickjs-ffi-types`, and `@jitl/quickjs-wasmfile-release-sync` version 0.32.0. These use the MIT license; original notices are retained within `quickjs-runtime/` and `licenses/upstream/quickjs-runtime/`. Both archive and complete member inventory are verified.
- Pandoc: the unmodified standalone executable supplied by the pinned Windows `pypandoc-binary` wheel or the reviewed official macOS Pandoc 3.9 archive. GPL version 2 or later and component notices are preserved in `licenses/pandoc/COPYING.md` and `licenses/pandoc/COPYRIGHT`. Source for Pandoc 3.9 is available at https://github.com/jgm/pandoc/tree/3.9 and https://hackage.haskell.org/package/pandoc-3.9/pandoc-3.9.tar.gz. Pandoc runs as a separate converter process.
- Typst 0.15.0: native Python wheel for the target platform. Original Typst and third-party notices are retained with its wheel distribution. It is used as the PDF compiler, without downloading packages at application startup.
- Fonts: the original Matplotlib TrueType font directory, including DejaVu, STIX, Computer Modern and LastResort, is copied unchanged into `fonts/`. Its original font notices and the full Matplotlib binary-distribution license are retained with the Matplotlib distribution and in `licenses/upstream/python/`. PDF text uses the unmodified Pretendard 1.3.9 Regular and Bold TrueType fonts under SIL Open Font License 1.1, bundled with the engine's `paper_factory/fonts/` assets, original license and exact npm archive/member provenance. That license is also preserved in the runtime license inventory. No host font installation is required.

Build and download commands are maintainer-only. Installed apps use the packaged interpreter, Node, QuickJS, converter and fonts; they do not install dependencies, copy a developer virtual environment, or substitute a system PATH runtime. The file inventory binds all runtime payload bytes to an inventory SHA256 stored separately in the packaged application's `third-party/runtime-inventory-binding.json`.

Windows is verified by actually importing native dependencies and running QuickJS and document-conversion diagnostics. A foreign-platform assembly, including a macOS payload assembled on Windows, is not a native installation or execution test.
